scientificBasis.finding: Initial ball/wheel position, velocity and acceleration can contain predictive information on a physical European roulette under suitable conditions; Small and Tse reported at least 18% expected return in their experiment.
A quantitative roulette study used 10,980 real online-casino wheel outcomes with backtesting and walk-forward optimization, motivating strict temporal validation.

fairNullControl.interpretation: A favorable point estimate on random data was correctly rejected once uncertainty and the actual break-even threshold were applied.

controlledPhysicalSignal.construction: Synthetic outcome location was deliberately made dependent on current-spin phase, ball period, rotor period, deceleration proxy and direction. It is a positive-control signal, not a claim about any casino wheel.

realWorldPromotionRequirements: ball and rotor visible before bet close
confidence lower bound above exact payout break-even threshold
